headline: Two players placed on NHL waivers for Nov. 4
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Columbus Blue Jackets forward Danton Heinen and defenseman Emil Andrae were placed on waivers on Wednesday.

The numbers back up why CBJ would shuffle the bottom of the roster. Heinen has no points in 10 games so far this season, and his own expected goals (the quality of his shots and chances) total 1.41, so he's been unlucky as well as quiet. The bigger issue is that CBJ controlled 44 percent of the expected goals at 5-on-5 with him on the ice, about four points worse than the team does without him. Andrae's sample is only five games, with two assists, and the team does slightly better with him out there, though he has generated almost nothing himself. Drafted 54th overall by the Flyers in 2020, he spent last season in Philadelphia. CBJ sit at 6-7-0 and have controlled 45 percent of the expected goals overall. A goaltending bump (3.6 goals saved above expected) is holding that together, so depth decisions that tilt the underlying play even slightly matter here. Neither player looks like a fantasy factor, and the waiver wire is the likelier destination for both.
